text:
## Observations

1. Transposing the grid preserves edge adjacency and the count. The shorter side has length at most 14 because the grid has at most 200 cells.
2. In row-major order, the only already processed neighbors of a cell are the cells immediately above and to its left, when they exist.
3. One digit per column records the most recently processed cell in that column. At any cut, the nonempty entries form at most two contiguous row segments, and consecutive digits within each segment must differ.
4. Two partial fillings with the same recorded digits have the same valid continuations, so their counts can be added modulo 998244353.

## Solution sketch

> Transposing the grid preserves edge adjacency and the count. The shorter side has length at most 14 because the grid has at most 200 cells.

1. Orient the grid so its width \(w\) is the shorter side. Keep a map from frontier states to counts, where a frontier state stores one digit per column. Use a sentinel digit 0 for columns that have no processed cell yet. Initialize the all-zero state with count 1.

> In row-major order, the only already processed neighbors of a cell are the cells immediately above and to its left, when they exist.

2. Process the cells from left to right, one row at a time. At column \(j\), the old entry for \(j\) is the digit above, and the entry for \(j-1\) is the digit to the left if \(j\) is beyond the first column. Try only the given digit for a fixed cell, or all three digits for a `?`. Discard any choice equal to an existing neighbor. For each surviving choice, replace entry \(j\) with the chosen digit and add the old state's count to that state in a fresh map. The sentinel handles the first row, and skipping the left check in the first column also handles single-column grids.

> Two partial fillings with the same recorded digits have the same valid continuations, so their counts can be added modulo 998244353.

3. Reduce every addition modulo 998244353. After processing the last cell, sum the remaining counts modulo the same number and print the result. Each valid filling contributes once through its sequence of digit choices. If a fixed digit makes every continuation impossible, the map becomes empty and the result is 0.

> One digit per column records the most recently processed cell in that column. At any cut, the nonempty entries form at most two contiguous row segments, and consecutive digits within each segment must differ.

4. A segment of length \(k\) has at most \(3\cdot 2^{k-1}\) digit sequences, since its first digit has three choices and each later digit has at most two. With at most two segments and at most \(w\) recorded digits, each map has \(O(2^w)\) entries. Pack each digit into two bits of an integer so that inspecting or replacing an entry takes constant time. With at most three choices per state, the algorithm takes \(O(HW\,2^w)\) expected time using hash maps and \(O(2^w)\) auxiliary space beyond the grid.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
